Dots page the reel; each card offers one follow-up, because an insight worth surfacing is worth asking about.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: trim-panel
items.title: Trim Panel
items.description: The inspector with an agent's hands on it: width, height, radius, and opacity read out as rolling numerals while the stage element re-trims live on the glide spring — every adjustment narrated, because a tool that changes your design silently is indistinguishable from a bug. The fields are the record, the stage is the proof, and the two cannot disagree: both read from the same values.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: blue-pencil
items.title: Blue Pencil
items.description: The editor's blue pencil: select a passage and a small toolbar of rewrite verbs springs up anchored to the selection — explain, improve, shorten, tone. The verbs hand the selected text back out; the pencil never rewrites anything itself, because the surface that edits and the model that edits must be separable for either to be trusted.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: workbench-rail
items.title: Workbench Rail
items.description: The workspace rail: primary destinations, then the running conversations, with one gliding highlight that travels to whatever the pointer is over — a single shared element, so the hover reads as one light moving rather than many lighting up. The invite quota is a printed fraction, not a paywall surprise, and the whole rail folds to a spine when the work needs the width back.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-app-window
items.title: App Window Vignette
items.description: A product window that paints itself in: the chrome lands first, sidebar rows cascade, the spark line draws its series, and the headline number rolls up on the readout — the standard product-demo vignette for a hero that wants to show software working without shipping a screenshot. Purely presentational: the scene reads to assistive tech as one image with an honest label.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-handset
items.title: Handset Vignette
items.description: A handset with an app scene scrolling on a slow loop — the mobile-demo vignette for a hero that wants to show the phone view without a video file. The card list is doubled and translated by half, so the loop never jumps; hovering rests the scroll, because a reader leaning in deserves a still page.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-exchange
items.title: Exchange Vignette
items.description: A chat moment that loops politely: bubbles land one beat at a time, the finished exchange rests long enough to be read whole, then it clears and begins again. A vignette, not a chat — the beats are fixed, nothing is interactive, and the scene reads to assistive tech as one image with the transcript as its label. The working thread is volley-thread.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-voice-note
items.title: Voice Note Vignette
items.description: A voice note as a scene: speaker, a fixed waveform, and a play head that sweeps the bars — each brightening as the head passes, the way a message app renders playback. The waveform is provided data, not audio analysis, and nothing plays; it is the shape of a voice for heroes about talking to software.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-search-lens
items.title: Search Lens Vignette
items.description: A search moment: the field focuses, the query types itself, three results settle in, the scene rests, then it clears and runs again. A vignette of finding — fixed beats, nothing interactive, one image to assistive tech — for heroes about products where the answer is a search away. The working palette is command-deck; this is its portrait.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-hub
items.title: Hub Vignette
items.description: A centre node with its services arranged on a ring, links drawn from each to the core and a pulse travelling every line in turn — the integration scene, for heroes about products that sit in the middle of other tools. Positions are computed from index and count, so the layout is identical on server and client, and the pulse order is fixed.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-file-run
items.title: File Run Vignette
items.description: Files flowing a drawn path into a destination, one departing at a time, with the landed tally rolling on the readout — the ingestion scene, for heroes about pipelines and imports. Departures are a mount-driven cycle and the tally counts landings honestly: it only rolls when a chip arrives.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-wave-meter
items.title: Wave Meter Vignette
items.description: A metering loop: bars breathe through a fixed pattern that rotates, with one peak marked and named — the live-signal scene, for heroes about telemetry and throughput. The pattern is data, the rotation is a mount-driven cycle, and nothing is random, so server and client always paint the same meter.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-iso-stack
items.title: Iso Stack Vignette
items.description: An isometric stack rising into place, each layer labelled on its edge — the architecture scene, for heroes that want layers of a system without a diagramming tool. Plates are CSS-transformed divs, so they theme like everything else and cost nothing to load.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-iso-floor
items.title: Iso Floor Vignette
items.description: An isometric tile floor with a route pulsing across it, one tile at a time — the infrastructure scene, for heroes about things moving through a system. The floor is a CSS-rotated grid, the route is fixed data, and the pulse is a mount-driven cycle: deterministic everywhere.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: bubble-pop
items.title: Bubble Pop
items.description: A sheet of bubble wrap you actually get to pop: every bubble is a real button, each press squashes it flat with a crisp snap and a four-fleck puff, and the counter underneath keeps honest score. Pop them all and the sheet takes a breath, then re-inflates in a cascade — because the only thing better than bubble wrap is more bubble wrap.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: poke-pudding
items.title: Poke Pudding
items.description: A pudding with a face and opinions about being poked. Press and it squashes; release and it jiggles back on a real spring; poke it three times fast and it goes briefly dizzy before composing itself. Not a physics simulation — a character, which is why the eyes matter more than the wobble.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: stamp-pad
items.title: Stamp Pad
items.description: A blank sheet and a tray of stamps: click anywhere and the next stamp slams down at that exact spot — oversized, slightly rotated, thunking to rest with an impact ring. Rotations and colors cycle from fixed tables, the sheet holds two dozen before it clears itself, and keyboard users stamp a tidy grid of their own.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: cookie-bite
items.title: Cookie Bite
items.description: A cookie you eat one click at a time: five bites disappear from the rim in a fixed order through an SVG mask, each with a startle squash and three crumbs arcing to the plate. When it is gone, the plate admits “worth it” — and a fresh one springs in, because grief should be brief.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: hatchling
items.title: Hatchling
items.description: An egg that hatches in three taps: the first jolts a crack into it, the second chips the shell, and the third pops the top so a chick can rise, look both ways, and wink. A fourth tap tucks everything back in for the next visitor. The caption underplays the whole thing, which is the correct amount of ceremony.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: yo-yo-drop
items.title: Yo-yo Drop
items.description: A yo-yo that sleeps while you hold and rewinds when you let go: press and the disc drops the string's length and spins in place, string faintly humming; release and it climbs home on a crisp spring with one small settle bounce. Hold too long and it wobbles — it has somewhere to be. The caption keeps score in three words or fewer.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: soap-bubble
items.title: Soap Bubble
items.description: A wand you blow through by holding: the film grows from the ring with an iridescent sheen and a nervous wobble, and on release the bubble detaches, drifts up a gentle S, and pops into droplets at the top of its rise. Release too early and it just wisps out — bubbles have standards. Two in flight at most; patience is part of the toy.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: applause-hold
items.title: Applause Hold
items.description: Press-and-hold applause that builds: the hands clap faster the longer you hold, the meter fills, and at four seconds it tips into a standing ovation — glow, flecks, the works. Release and the ovation drains politely. Where the heart tap is a single thank-you, this is the whole room getting to its feet.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: tea-dunk
items.title: Tea Dunk
items.description: A mug and a teabag on a string: drag it under and ripples ring the entry, lift it out and it drips, and the water deepens toward amber as it steeps. Park it and wait, or dunk like you mean it — full dunks steep faster, which is the toy quietly rewarding enthusiasm. At full steep the surface steams and the caption declares it done.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: balloon-pump
items.title: Balloon Pump
items.description: A hand pump, a balloon, and the outcome everyone is waiting for: each press drives the plunger, sends a puff down the hose, and stretches the balloon one stage larger — trembling faintly at stage five, gone at six in a fling of rubber scraps. A beat later the next colour is on the nozzle, deflated and optimistic. The pop is anticipated, earned, and immediately forgiven.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: top-spin
items.title: Top Spin
items.description: A spinning top with honest physics feel: flick it and it spins with your velocity, coasts down on fixed friction, enters the death wobble every top owes its audience, and tips over with one rock. Click a fallen top and it stands back up, ready to go again. The caption narrates in four states and never oversells.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: clack-beads
items.title: Clack Beads
items.description: Five beads on a rod: flick the free one into the cluster and the impact travels — the struck bead compresses, a clack tick flashes at contact, and the far bead shoots out, coasts, and wanders lazily back. Not a physics engine; an authored choreography tuned until it feels like one, which is cheaper and never misses. The pendulum cousin lives elsewhere — these slide.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pinwheel-breeze
items.title: Pinwheel Breeze
items.description: A paper pinwheel that spins from the breeze your cursor makes: pointer speed becomes angular velocity, friction takes it back, and at rest it sways like something waiting outside a shop. Fast enough and the vanes blend into a blur disc. A click gives it a push, so the breeze is never the only way to play.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: kite-tug
items.title: Kite Tug
items.description: A diamond kite bobbing on a sagging line — tug it and the line snaps taut, the kite dives, swoops a loop with its tail streaming, and settles back into the idle sky. The line is one quadratic path whose sag breathes with the kite; the rope simulation lives elsewhere in the catalog, and this scene does not need it. The caption says “wheee” exactly once per swoop.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: paper-plane
items.title: Paper Plane
items.description: A folded dart that launches from its pad, climbs, banks, dips, loops once, and glides home to stick the landing — with a dashed trail drawing in behind it and fading after touchdown. The whole lap is one authored flight; a second loop is a prop away. For empty states, sent-confirmations, and anyone who misses classrooms.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: crank-tune
items.title: Crank Tune
items.description: A music box you crank by hand: drag the knob in circles and the arm tracks your pointer exactly, emitting a note glyph every quarter turn that floats up and away. Crank backwards and it plays nothing — the box is honest about which direction music comes from. Enter turns it a quarter turn for anyone playing by keyboard.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: gumball-run
items.title: Gumball Run
items.description: A gumball machine that actually delivers: turn the knob and a ball leaves the globe, rides the chute on an authored path, and bounces into the tray where the count ticks up. Colours cycle in fixed order, the globe visibly empties, and when it runs dry it restocks in a cascade. Three balls may be in transit before the machine asks you to wait.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: toast-pop
items.title: Toast Pop
items.description: A toaster that makes you wait for it: push the lever, the bread sinks, the slot glows, the crust browns, and just before the end the whole machine gives one small shudder of anticipation. Then it leaps, lands askew, sheds crumbs, and takes a topping stamp. The suspense is the feature — a toaster that popped instantly would be a notification, and the catalog has those.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pull-cord
items.title: Pull Cord
items.description: A pendant lamp with a cord you actually pull: drag the bead down and the cord stretches under your hand, release past the threshold and the room floods warm — the cord snapping back into a couple of swings while dust motes drift up through the light. Let go short of the threshold and nothing happens, which is exactly what a real cord does.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: domino-run
items.title: Domino Run
items.description: A row of dominoes and one honest click: the first tile goes over, the topple propagates down the line on a cascade stagger with a dust puff at each base, and the last one raises a little flag. A beat later they all stand back up in reverse, ready to go again. The whole run is index math — no physics, no randomness, and it never fails to finish.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: googly-eyes
items.title: Googly Eyes
items.description: A pair of stick-on plastic eyes that follow your cursor with a slight spring lag, blink on their own schedule (every third one a double), and go cross-eyed when you get too close to the bridge of their nose. Boop them and the pupils rattle loose before settling back to work. Nothing here re-renders — tracking rides motion values from a document listener.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: duckling-trail
items.title: Duckling Trail
items.description: A pond where a mother duck follows your pointer and her ducklings conga behind her, each one springing off the last so the line bunches at rest and stretches when she moves. Leave the pond and the family drifts to the bank to wait. Arrow keys and Enter walk her between waypoints, because the toy should not need a mouse.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: tail-wag
items.title: Tail Wag
items.description: A dog behind a button whose tail wags faster the closer your cursor gets — a lazy sway across the room, a blur of enthusiasm up close. Press the button and the whole body joins in: rump shimmy, ears up, one heart. The caption escalates from “good dog” to “GOOD DOG”, which is the entire joke and it lands every time.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: critter-choir
items.title: Critter Choir
items.description: Four round critters in a row, each with its own pitch: tap one and it inflates, opens its mouth, and sends a note glyph rising — higher and lighter as you move up the scale. Tap all four inside a second and a half and they harmonize, notes fanning out over a glow. At rest they breathe slightly out of sync, which is most of the charm.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: little-door
items.title: Little Door
items.description: A tiny door in the baseboard and whoever lives behind it. Two knocks rattle the frame and move the caption along; the third cracks it open on its hinge, a pair of eyes blinks out, and a beat later it slams — shaking dust from the frame and leaving one word of review. Swap the resident for a flower if you would rather be greeted than judged.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pinata-tap
items.title: Piñata Tap
items.description: A piñata on a rope that takes five swings: each hit sends it swinging harder, tears another fringe strip loose, and moves the caption one word closer to inevitable. The fifth splits it open and a dozen candies arc out on authored gravity to land scattered on the floor. A beat later a fresh one drops in, because the only correct number of piñatas is another one.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: gift-unwrap
items.title: Gift Unwrap
items.description: A wrapped present that opens in two beats: the first click pulls the ribbon loose and slides the bands off, the second pops the lid tumbling away as the gift rises on a glow. A third re-wraps it with the next gift queued. Making the ribbon its own beat is the whole trick — unwrapping in one click is a reveal, unwrapping in two is a gift.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: medal-swing
items.title: Medal Swing
items.description: A medal that drops in on its lanyard, swings itself to rest on a decaying tween, and then keeps catching the light on a slow glint cycle. Hover for an extra flash; click because nobody can leave a hanging medal alone. Three tiers, each tinted from the palette rather than painted gold, so it belongs to whatever theme it lands in.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: high-five
items.title: High Five
items.description: An open palm waiting to be met: click and a second hand swings in, the two connect with a shockwave ring and a scatter of impact flecks, then part again. Double-tap too fast and the incoming hand whiffs straight past — the caption calls it, which is funnier than landing it. At rest the palm just breathes and invites.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: level-chime
items.title: Level Chime
items.description: An experience bar that levels up properly: each tap adds XP with a floating chip, and on filling, a shine sweeps the track, the bar drains, the readout carries the level up, a badge flips, and sparks ring out. Taps during the ceremony queue rather than drop — a progress toy that loses your taps is a bug wearing a costume.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: streak-flame
items.title: Streak Flame
items.description: A streak counter whose flame grows with the number: body and core flicker on the same period but different phases, so the two never sync and the whole thing reads alive. Extending it surges the flame and lifts embers; milestones flare. Break the streak and it gutters out to a wisp of smoke, which is exactly as unpleasant as it should be.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: glint-trophy
items.title: Glint Trophy
items.description: A shelf of four trophies that slide up on arrival and then take turns catching the light — one glint at a time, on a calm cycle, never two at once. Polish one and it wiggles, sparkles, and stays permanently a little brighter, so the shelf quietly records what you have fussed over. Dusting resets the whole thing.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: fortune-crack
items.title: Fortune Crack
items.description: A fortune cookie that squeezes, snaps into two settled halves, drops three crumbs, and unfurls a paper slip with a dry line printed on it. Click again and it re-fuses with the next fortune queued. The fortunes are workplace-plain rather than mystical, which makes them land.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: spark-jar
items.title: Spark Jar
items.description: Fireflies drifting across a dark card and a jar to catch them in: click one and it breaks from its drift, flies to the jar mouth, and settles inside bobbing while the glass glows one step warmer. Fill it and the lid taps shut, the jar blooms, and a moment later everything streams back out — the toy is a loop, not a wall.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: grow-sprout
items.title: Grow Sprout
items.description: A seed you water into a flower, one click at a time: droplets fall, a stem draws upward, leaves unfurl, and a bud swells and blooms six petals in a cascade. A fifth click drops a seed back into the soil and the plant fades, leaving the cycle ready to run again. Growth staged as clicks rather than time, so nobody has to wait to see the bloom.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: dodge-button
items.title: Dodge Button
items.description: A button that plays hard to get exactly twice, then relents — approach it with a pointer and it springs to the next seat in a fixed cycle, and after two dodges it returns to centre and lets you click it. Keyboard users are never dodged, and neither are touch devices, because a button that runs away from a thumb is not a joke, it is a bug.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: oracle-orb
items.title: Oracle Orb
items.description: A fortune-telling orb with the mysticism removed: shake it and the fluid clouds, the die surfaces, and an answer fades in that sounds like it came from a colleague rather than a spirit. Answers cycle in fixed order, so a demo tells everyone the same fortunes in the same sequence — which is the only honest way to run an oracle.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: mood-gem
items.title: Mood Gem
items.description: A faceted gem that reads the room from how you move: quick passes make it restless, slow ones calm it, sitting still turns it content, and leaving makes it still. It rotates almost imperceptibly so the facets keep catching differently, and clicking sets the current mood for a few seconds regardless of what your hands do next.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: disco-floor
items.title: Disco Floor
items.description: A small dance floor that lights under your cursor with a soft falloff and, left alone for a moment, starts dancing on its own through authored patterns — sweeps, checkers, a pulse from the centre. Move back in and it yields to you immediately. Clicking drops a beat: everything flashes, then falls back in a cascade.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: drum-pads
items.title: Drum Pads
items.description: Four squashy pads that hit like the real thing: each squashes under the strike and throws a burst matched to its voice — a thick ring for the kick, sharp lines for the snare, a fine spray for the hat, staggered arcs for the clap. Hit one repeatedly and the bursts grow. A strip beneath keeps the last eight hits, so you can see the groove you just played.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: snow-shake
items.title: Snow Shake
items.description: A snow globe you shake by click or by drag, where the settling is the point: flakes lift off the drift, swirl on seeded paths, and come down staggered until the last one lands and the caption says so. Every flake's path is derived from its index, so the same shake happens for everyone — a snow globe with no randomness in it at all.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: zen-rake
items.title: Zen Rake
items.description: A sand garden and a three-tooth comb: drag and three parallel grooves follow your hand, offset along the path normal so the rake reads as a rake. Strokes rest for a few seconds and then heal, the bed holding only its last six so it never silts up. Arrow keys rake too, for anyone gardening from the keyboard.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: wind-chimes
items.title: Wind Chimes
items.description: Five graduated tubes that sway from the breeze your cursor makes, each on its own natural period so they never move in unison — that desync is the entire effect. Contacts with the clapper flash in sequence rather than at once, and a click plays a full run down the scale. The caption names the weather you are making.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ferris-glow
items.title: Ferris Glow
items.description: A little ferris wheel turning at dusk, with the detail that matters: the cabins counter-rotate so they stay level however far the wheel has come around. Cabin and rim lights pulse on offset phases so the whole thing twinkles instead of blinking, hovering speeds the turn, and a click lights every bulb at once before they settle back in a cascade.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: sky-bloom
items.title: Sky Bloom
items.description: Fireworks you set off yourself: click anywhere in the night sky and a rocket rises from the skyline beneath your finger, decelerating to apex before blooming into twelve sparks that arc and droop under authored gravity. Three may be in the air at once, palettes cycle so consecutive shots differ, and the sky brightens a touch with each one.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: mail-fold
items.title: Mail Fold
items.description: A letter that folds itself into an envelope and leaves: the bottom third comes up, the top third comes down, a flap sweeps over, a seal presses on, and the whole thing tilts off the top-right corner trailing a dash of its own path. A fresh sheet drops in behind it. For sent-confirmations that deserve more than a checkmark.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: fridge-poetry
items.title: Fridge Poetry
items.description: Word magnets on a fridge door, draggable into whatever sentence you like — each lands on a loose grid with a small jiggle that sells the weight of the magnet, and the one you touched last sits on top. Arrow keys move them a cell at a time, because a drag-only toy quietly excludes half its audience.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: juggle-loop
items.title: Juggle Loop
items.description: Three balls in a proper cascade, each on the same authored arc offset by a third of the cycle, with hands that dip as they catch. Click to add a ball up to five — the tempo tightens to keep it plausible — and one more click drops the lot before starting over. Hovering runs it in slow motion, which is when you can see the pattern.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: rocket-drill
items.title: Rocket Drill
items.description: A launch with a countdown and, unusually, a recovery: three numerals pop while the rocket trembles harder, the gantry swings clear, it climbs out of frame on smoke, and then a parachute drifts the capsule back down to the pad. Most launch animations forget the coming-back part, which is the half that makes it a drill.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: claw-drop
items.title: Claw Drop
items.description: A claw machine that always catches — the honesty is the joke. The trolley sweeps the rail so you still have to time it, but wherever you stop, the claw takes the nearest plush, lifts it, and delivers it down the chute to the tray. Clear the bed and it restocks. No odds, no coins, no disappointment.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: quest-log
items.title: Quest Log
items.description: A quest list built to be finished: each advance rolls its counter and fills its bar, and completing one sweeps the row, flies its reward to the running total, and unlocks the next quest in the chain. The unlock is the hook — a log that opens its own next line is harder to close than one that simply ends.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: skill-tree
items.title: Skill Tree
items.description: A talent tree you spend points into: available nodes pulse for attention, spending one fills the node, draws the link from its parent, and cascades any newly-eligible node into reach. The capstone sweeps the whole tree. Respec drains it all back in reverse, because a build you cannot undo is a build nobody experiments with.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: rank-insignia
items.title: Rank Insignia
items.description: A rank badge that promotes with the ceremony a promotion deserves: the old insignia clears in a flash, the new one lands on a spring, a chevron stamps on, light sweeps the plate, and the name rolls over. Five tiers, and an honest ceiling at the top instead of invented infinite ranks.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: combo-meter
items.title: Combo Meter
items.description: A combo counter that drains while you watch, so every hit is relief as much as reward: landing one refills the bar, pops the numeral, and steps the multiplier at fixed thresholds — which shortens the fuse. Let it empty and the combo shatters, the panel cools, and your best score stays on screen as the reason to go again.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: daily-check
items.title: Daily Check
items.description: The seven-day check-in strip, built as a chain: claiming a day fills it, stamps it, flies its reward to the total, draws a connector to tomorrow, and hands the pulse to the next tile. Day seven pays out and the week rolls over with the streak intact. It never reads the clock — days are indexes, so the strip renders identically on the server and every visit.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: loot-chest
items.title: Loot Chest
items.description: A chest that spends longer on the anticipation than the payoff: it shudders three times with rising amplitude, the clasp pops, light leaks from the seam, and only then does the lid swing and the beam erupt. The card that rises carries a rarity, and the reaction scales with it — legendary earns the sweep, common earns a settle and nothing more.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: prize-wheel
items.title: Prize Wheel
items.description: A segmented wheel whose last half-second is the whole experience: a wind-up counter-rotation, several turns, then a hard deceleration onto the segment with the pointer ticking slower as it goes. The blank segment lands flat on purpose — muted caption, no sparks — because a wheel that celebrates nothing is a wheel nobody reads.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pack-tear
items.title: Pack Tear
items.description: A foil pack you actually tear: the rip tracks your drag one-to-one, shedding flecks, and commits past two thirds. Five cards fan out face-down, and each flip is its own verdict with rarity-scaled reaction. The haul line totals what you pulled, then a fresh pack reseals with the next set queued.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: gacha-capsule
items.title: Gacha Capsule
items.description: A capsule machine with the full ritual: crank it round, watch the capsule bounce down the chute, wobble to rest, crack along its seam, and present what is inside. Tiers cycle in fixed order and the top one is deliberately infrequent — a machine that hands out rainbows every turn is not a machine anyone remembers.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: reward-track
items.title: Reward Track
items.description: The season track, built around its real mechanic: the unclaimed counter. Progress advances a head along the ribbon, nodes it passes start pulsing, and the nag ticks up until you claim them. Milestones every fifth node pay bigger, and finishing the track offers the next season rather than pretending the run goes on forever.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: leaderboard-climb
items.title: Leaderboard Climb
items.description: A leaderboard whose whole point is the row with your name on it: score a round and the list resorts, your row physically travelling past the ones it overtook and nudging each on the way. The rival directly above you is named and marked, because a target you can read is worth more than a rank you cannot.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: versus-bar
items.title: Versus Bar
items.description: A tug-of-war between two sides on a single bar: each push moves the seam, consecutive pushes build a surge that pushes further, and a push the other way resets it — which is where the drama lives. Crossing the centre names the new leader, and past eighty percent the losing side starts showing the brink.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: bracket-run
items.title: Bracket Run
items.description: An eight-entrant elimination bracket that plays out one match at a time: both slots tense, the loser dims and strikes through, and the winner's name travels the connector into the next round as the line draws in behind it. Outcomes come from a fixed table — a bracket that reseeds itself every visit cannot be reasoned about.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: score-tick
items.title: Score Tick
items.description: An arcade scoreboard with tiered juice: bigger points pop harder, throw more flecks, and float a larger chip, so a thousand lands differently from fifty. Consecutive presses build a chain that decays on its own. Passing the high score is the beat the whole component is built around, and it gets the room it deserves.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: podium-rise
items.title: Podium Rise
items.description: A results podium that reveals in reverse — third, second, first — because saving the winner is the entire dramaturgy. Plinths rise, cards land, scores roll up from zero, and first place takes an overshoot, a crown, and a sweep. Clicking mid-ceremony skips to the finish: a results screen that traps you is a bad results screen.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: timing-bar
items.title: Timing Bar
items.description: The bar every crafting game teaches you to hit: a marker sweeps, you stop it, and the hit-test reads the marker's live motion value rather than any state — which is what makes the judgement honest. The perfect zone sits deliberately off-centre so it has to be learned, and every success speeds the next sweep while narrowing the target.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: rhythm-tap
items.title: Rhythm Tap
items.description: A single lane, an authored sixteen-step pattern, and a hit zone: notes arrive on the beat and you tap them, judged perfect, good, or missed against a step clock rather than any DOM position. Combo, best, and a rolling accuracy figure sit above it. It starts paused, so nothing moves until someone asks it to.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: accuracy-ring
items.title: Accuracy Ring
items.description: A ring shrinking toward a target you tap when they match — and then it tells you the signed error in pixels, so you learn whether you are early or late. That readout is the whole teaching device. Success speeds the next ring and narrows the band; a miss resets both.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: power-gauge
items.title: Power Gauge
items.description: Hold to charge, release to commit — and the needle does not stop at full, it oscillates, so overcharging is a real risk and waiting for the second pass is a real strategy. The sweet spot sits below maximum on purpose: max power is a trap, and the overcharge result is visibly worse than a good one.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: reflex-light
items.title: Reflex Light
items.description: Five lights arm one at a time, hold, and go out together — that blackout is the signal. Timing comes from event timestamps, never the wall clock, and a click before the lights drop is a jump start that voids the attempt. The penalty is what makes the wait tense.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: energy-pips
items.title: Energy Pips
items.description: The energy economy that decides when someone comes back: pips drain as they are spent and refill on a timer that only runs while the bank is below full. At zero the wait is stated plainly rather than hidden, because an honest countdown is the mechanic. Nothing here reads the wall clock — the countdown is an interval tick counter, so it renders the same on the server.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: health-shield
items.title: Health Shield
items.description: A damage model built for legibility: shield absorbs first and shatters when it breaks, then health takes the rest — leaving a chip ghost at the old value that drains a beat later, so you can see exactly what the hit cost. Low health warms the fill and adds a pulse; healing refuses to overfill with a visible bounce at the cap.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: mana-orb
items.title: Mana Orb
items.description: A glass orb of liquid mana whose surface actually moves: two wave layers at different periods, deliberately desynced, because a single sine reads as a machine and two read as liquid. Casting drops the level and sloshes it, an empty cast is refused as clearly as a successful one lands, and regen shimmers until full and then stops.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: cooldown-dial
items.title: Cooldown Dial
items.description: Four abilities with four different cooldowns, which is what gives an ability bar its polyrhythm: each casts, dims, and unwinds its own radial sweep back to ready, with a brief shared lockout after any cast so mashing gains nothing. The return to ready gets its own pop, because the wait is only worth it if the reward is felt.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: boss-meter
items.title: Boss Meter
items.description: A long fight made legible by its thresholds: the bar carries phase markers, and crossing one stops everything for a beat, stamps the numeral, warms the tint, and names what just changed. That pause is the device — without it a boss bar is just a slow health bar. The last phase enrages, and defeat shatters it.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: sticker-album
items.title: Sticker Album
items.description: An album page whose empty slots do the asking: each collect flies a sticker to its place, presses it down at a slightly crooked angle, and solidifies the outline. Every fourth pull is a duplicate that slides off to the spares tray — a set you complete without ever pulling a double is not a collection, it is a checklist.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: badge-case
items.title: Badge Case
items.description: A case of achievements where the locked ones still say what they are: a silhouette, a lock, and the hint that would earn it — because a hidden name teaches nothing about what to chase. One secret badge is the right number. Each unlock fills the medallion, flips the glyph, and prints the share of players who hold it.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: passport-stamps
items.title: Passport Stamps
items.description: A passport leaf that takes a stamp per destination: the head descends, the page shudders, the mark presses in a degree or two off true, and ink spreads at the edges. A filled page turns to a fresh one. Dates are pre-formatted strings and nothing reads a clock, so the page renders identically everywhere.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: set-complete
items.title: Set Complete
items.description: Five cards and a bonus that stays locked until the last one lands. Empty frames show exactly what is missing, connectors draw between placed cards so the set visibly links up, and completion lights the chain, sheens every card, and breaks the lock off the bonus. Pulling a card back re-locks it just as clearly — the loss has to read or the set means nothing.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pet-companion
items.title: Pet Companion
items.description: A companion that grows through four stages as your bond rises — and droops, curls up, and dims when it falls, because a pet that cannot be neglected is a toy rather than a companion. Feeding and playing restore it visibly, it blinks on its own, and the mood line always says plainly where you stand.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: journey-map
items.title: Journey Map
items.description: A winding campaign path where the road lights up behind you: the avatar travels an authored waypoint route while a dash-clipped overlay follows it exactly, so progress reads as ground covered rather than a bar filling. Each arrival pops its milestone, hands the pulse to the next, and names what was reached.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: season-track
items.title: Season Track
items.description: A two-lane season pass with a closing window: free and premium rows across eight tiers, an unclaimed counter that nags, and a retroactive payout when premium unlocks — which is exactly why the pattern works, shown honestly. Ending the season expires everything unclaimed, in view, because the expiry is the whole point of a season.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: territory-grid
items.title: Territory Grid
items.description: A board two sides expand across, where you may only claim tiles touching what you already hold — so the frontier, not the whole grid, is the decision. Claims ripple into their neighbours, surrounding an enemy tile captures it, and the opponent answers from a fixed sequence so the same board plays the same way for everyone.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ladder-climb
items.title: Ladder Climb
items.description: A competitive ladder you can fall down, which is the only reason climbing it matters: promotions light the band and unfurl a banner, demotions dim it and say so plainly with no sparks and no ceremony. A demotion shield absorbs the first loss at the bottom of a division, so the fall reads as fair rather than arbitrary.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: checkpoint-run
items.title: Checkpoint Run
items.description: A run measured in ground covered, with flags that plant as you pass them and a stumble that throws you back to the last one — quickly, and a little ugly, because losing ground should not look graceful. Progress that cannot be lost is not progress, it is a countdown; the best distance persists so you always have your own mark to beat.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: crit-hit
items.title: Crit Hit
items.description: Damage numbers that scale their weight with what they mean: a graze drifts, a hit rises, a crit punches in with a starburst and a shake, and a crush brings the whole card with it. Numbers fan out along a cycled vector table so a flurry stays readable instead of stacking into a smear. The tier order is fixed, so the same strikes always read the same.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: streak-heat
items.title: Streak Heat
items.description: Escalation you can feel: each multiplier tier warms the panel, grows the numeral, and adds one more ambient layer on top of the last — a pulse, then a shimmer, then a rotating glow, then heat haze. Breaking the streak cools everything down over a slower tween than it took to heat, because a loss should take its time.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: perfect-stamp
items.title: Perfect Stamp
items.description: The verdict, slammed onto the results card: it arrives fast and oversized, lands hard at a slight angle, throws a shockwave and dust, and shudders the card by an amount scaled to the grade. A perfect run earns a sweep and a glow. A failed one gets a dull thud and no celebration, because a results screen that congratulates failure teaches nothing.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: impact-frame
items.title: Impact Frame
items.description: Hit-stop, demonstrated and measured: an impact freezes the scene for a set number of milliseconds, flashes, jolts within its own bounds, and prints the freeze duration so the effect can be studied rather than just felt. A compare toggle runs the same strike without the freeze, which is the fastest way to understand why it matters.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: xp-shower
items.title: XP Shower
items.description: Reward that arrives as objects: orbs burst from the source, hang for a beat, then stream to the counter on staggered arcs — and the total climbs in steps as each one lands, which is the entire reason to do this instead of animating a number. The big orbs are saved for last, because pacing is most of the payoff.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: avatar-forge
items.title: Avatar Forge
items.description: A character maker where only the layer you changed moves — cycle a head, and the head pops while everything else holds, so the eye lands on the edit instead of hunting for it. A handle is derived from the current combination and rewrites itself as parts change, which is the small thing that turns a shape stack into someone. Saving stamps it into a roster of the last three busts.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: guild-crest
items.title: Guild Crest
items.description: Heraldry, assembled in order: the shield drops and settles, the field wipes across it, the charge stamps on with a ring, and the ribbon unfurls from the centre carrying the name. Each layer waits for the one before it, because a crest that arrives all at once is only an image — the sequence is the ceremony. Cycling a part re-runs that layer alone, and a mock blazon reads the whole device back in shorthand.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: team-roster
items.title: Team Roster
items.description: The lobby before the match, where the interesting state is always the person you are waiting on. Teammates ready themselves on a fixed schedule, one of them deliberately slow, one of them drifting away partway through — because readiness that ignores presence is a lie. When the last ring fills, the countdown runs and the rows pulse together.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: duel-ready
items.title: Duel Ready
items.description: The face-off screen, which people remember better than the match. Two sides slide in from opposite edges, a divider wipes between them, and the versus mark stamps in the centre; locking in lights your frame and leans your fighter toward the middle, the physical tell that you are committed. When both sides are in, they lunge, the mark flares, and the count runs down to the word.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: emote-wheel
items.title: Emote Wheel
items.description: Hold to bloom eight emotes out of the centre, sweep toward one, release to play it — and release near the middle to back out with nothing, because a wheel you cannot cancel is a trap. A cooldown unwinds on the trigger afterwards, which is not a limitation but the design that keeps the thing charming instead of turning it into a spam device.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: unlock-gate
items.title: Unlock Gate
items.description: The feature that stayed greyed out for a week, finally opening: the requirement meter fills, the padlock lifts and falls away, the plate splits down the middle, and the blur drops off something that was genuinely there the whole time. Short of the threshold the plate refuses — a shake, a rattle, and a caption — because a gate that never says no has taught nobody anything.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: prestige-reset
items.title: Prestige Reset
items.description: Trading everything you built for a mark that says you did it. The stats drain one row at a time, the level counts itself down, and then the whole panel goes quiet for a beat before the new star ignites — that held pause is the most important frame in the sequence. It confirms before it commits, which is not friction but the acknowledgement the ceremony runs on.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: tier-upgrade
items.title: Tier Upgrade
items.description: Status made physical: a membership card that flips into its next self, where the new face only ever comes around mid-flip and is never visible early. Each rung changes the material, the perk, and the figure, because a flip that lands on the card you already had is the exact failure this component exists to avoid. Stepping back flips the other way, so the direction of travel reads.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: mission-board
items.title: Mission Board
items.description: A board you take work FROM, which is a different instrument from a list of what you already hold: postings are pinned and unclaimed, the slots that hold them are few, and accepting one lifts it off its pin and carries it into a slot, leaving the hole behind so the board reads as depleted. With every slot full the board refuses — the card tugs against its pin and springs back.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: return-gift
items.title: Return Gift
items.description: The loop reaching back out: a parcel waiting because you were gone, whose box visibly grows richer with the length of the absence, so the reward is legible before it is ever opened. The ribbon unties, the lid tips away, and the gifts rise one at a time with the best one held back for last — the order of a reveal is most of the reward. The greeting is glad you are back and never once mentions how long it took.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: focus-rail
items.title: Focus Rail
items.description: The primitive behind expanding galleries and team panels: a row of panels where the one under the pointer, or holding focus, grows on a spring while its siblings contract in place. Leaving the rail always restores an expanded panel, because a rail with nothing open reads as broken. Hover expands by default; a press mode waits for a click or Enter, and the keyboard roves either way.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: turn-modal
items.title: Turn Modal
items.description: A card that lifts, travels to the centre, and turns over on Y into a focus-trapped dialog — the flip and the travel are one motion, so the dialog face comes around mid-flight and is never visible early. Closing reverses the same path back to the card. Where morph-dialog reshapes the trigger into the dialog, this one turns it over, which is the right device when the card and the dialog are two faces of the same object.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: elastic-type
items.title: Elastic Type
items.description: Display text whose glyphs compress under the cursor and rebound when it leaves — each letter its own spring, so a word behaves like a row of rubber blocks. The rebound overshoot on the way back is the signature; without it the effect reads as a squash, not an elastic. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: echo-type
items.title: Echo Type
items.description: Display text with echo layers stacked behind it that fan apart on hover and re-stack when the pointer leaves — fanning staggers outward from the lead, and closing reverses the stagger so the layers fold back like a deck. An always-on mode holds the fan open and breathes it. Built for 404 numerals and single-word headlines that need presence without a backdrop.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: band-type
items.title: Band Type
items.description: Display text sliced into horizontal bands that slip sideways under the cursor — the bands nearest the pointer travel furthest, and they alternate direction, which is what makes the word read as slipping rather than leaning. Leave, and the bands settle back top-down on a spring. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-empty-drawer
items.title: Vignette · Empty Drawer
items.description: The illustration for an empty archive: a quiet isometric filing cabinet whose top drawer springs open on a loop to show there is nothing in it, and extends a little further under the pointer. Built from clipped faces rather than 3D transforms, so it holds in every browser, and it pauses the moment it scrolls out of view.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-search-sweep
items.title: Vignette · Search Sweep
items.description: The illustration for no results: a lens roams down a short stack of result lines, and the lines part as it passes — the parting is the picture of nothing being there — before a small zero settles at the end. Every element rides one clock of authored keyframes, so the scene cannot drift apart the way independently timed loops do.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-inbox-zero
items.title: Vignette · Inbox Zero
items.description: The illustration for a cleared inbox: the flap opens, the last message lifts out and away, the badge counts down as each one leaves, and a check settles when it reads zero. The countdown is what makes the zero mean something — an envelope that is simply empty tells you nothing about the work that emptied it.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: vignette-blank-board
items.title: Vignette · Blank Board
items.description: The illustration for a first run: three empty columns, one starter card, and a cursor that picks it up and carries it across the board, dropping it into the last column where a dashed slot fills to receive it. The cursor and the card share one set of keyframes, so they travel as one thing rather than two things pretending to.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: surface-paint
items.title: Surface Paint
items.description: The stage every effect in this wing stands on: your interface renders real and interactive, the painter keeps a texture of it current, and an effect layer draws over it. Overlay mode keeps the DOM visible and draws only where the effect differs; replace mode holds the DOM at zero opacity — still in flow, still focusable, still in the accessibility tree — and shows the transformed texture in its place, with clicks passing straight through.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: crystal-lens
items.title: Crystal Lens
items.description: A lens that follows the cursor and refracts the live interface like a crystal ball: the texture bends toward the centre, the edge disperses into colour fringes, and a touch of frost softens the rim. Hover a heading or a control and the lens zooms on it. The proving effect of the wing — the DOM stays real and clickable underneath while a shader does the optics.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ascii-lens
items.title: ASCII Lens
items.description: A soft lens that follows the cursor and redraws the live interface beneath it as characters — glyphs chosen by the shape of what they cover, not just its brightness, so an edge reads as a slash and a fill as a block. Outside the lens the page is itself; inside it, the page is type. The DOM stays real and clickable throughout.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: dither-lens
items.title: Dither Lens
items.description: A lens that pixelates the live interface into an ordered dither — Bayer, halftone, hatch, or dash — with a two-colour palette and a click that sends a degauss ripple through it. Retro on purpose and exact about it: the pattern is a fixed matrix, so the same page always dithers the same way.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: cipher-surface
items.title: Cipher Surface
items.description: The interface renders as scrambled cipher glyphs until the cursor comes close, and decodes back into crisp, coloured UI behind a flickering wavefront. Idle glyphs reroll on a fixed cadence from a seeded table, so the scramble looks alive without ever being random. The real DOM is underneath the whole time.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: scanner-lens
items.title: Scanner Lens
items.description: A scanner that follows the cursor and magnifies the live interface inside a HUD reticle — ring, crosshair, ticks, corner brackets, and a mono readout of what it is over — with clicks that send a ripple bending across the page. Where the crystal lens is optics, this one is instrumentation.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: dust-reveal
items.title: Dust Reveal
items.description: The interface renders as fine grey dust — grains wandering from their home pixels, the brightest content scattering furthest — and coalesces into crisp, coloured UI where the cursor comes near, with a chromatic edge at the reveal. Idle grains drift on a seeded field, so the dust breathes without a single random number.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pond-glass
items.title: Pond Glass
items.description: The interface under still water. A click drops a stone: rings spread across the page, refracting and highlighting everything they cross, then settle. The waves are a real height-field simulation on the GPU with a byte-precision fallback, so it runs where half-float buffers are missing, and the page beneath stays clickable.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: rain-glass
items.title: Rain Glass
items.description: Rain on a window, with the interface behind it. Droplets bead on the pane and run in trails that bend the view, a haze softens what they do not cover, and the cursor wipes a clear patch that fogs back over. Every droplet is seeded from its cell, so the same pane always rains the same way.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ice-pane
items.title: Ice Pane
items.description: Frost across the interface that melts where the cursor rests and creeps back when it leaves. The frost is a crystalline field that blurs and refracts the view with a cold tint and a few glints; the melt is a persistent map that the pointer warms and time refreezes, with a wet rim at the boundary. The DOM stays live under the ice.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: warp-grid
items.title: Warp Grid
items.description: The interface as a grid of cells on springs. Move slowly and nothing happens; move fast and the cells you pass shear in the direction of travel, edges splitting into colour, then spring back into place. The field is simulated on the CPU at grid resolution and read by the shader as a texture, so it costs almost nothing.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: droplet-cursor
items.title: Droplet Cursor
items.description: A chain of droplets that trails the cursor and refracts the interface behind it. Each drop follows the one ahead, shrinking along the chain, and the drops merge as one liquid surface where they touch; light bends through them, catches on a highlight, and tints the rim. Draws only where the drops are, so the page is itself everywhere else.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: shield-field
items.title: Shield Field
items.description: A faint lattice over the interface that rings out when clicked: a shockwave travels from the point of impact, lighting each cell as it passes and bending the page a little under the front, then fades. Cells near the pointer glow softly. Draws only the lattice and the waves, so the page is itself everywhere else.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: signal-glitch
items.title: Signal Glitch
items.description: The interface as a weak signal. Bursts of interference tear it into shifted bands, split its colour channels, and speckle it with noise, then it reassembles — clean between bursts. The bursts are scheduled from a seeded clock, so the pattern is deterministic; a click forces one. Underneath, the page is live the whole time.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: tape-wear
items.title: Tape Wear
items.description: The interface played back from a worn cassette: chroma bleeding sideways, a faint vertical jitter, a tracking band that drifts up the frame tearing what it crosses, dropout streaks, scanlines, and a soft vignette. Every flaw is seeded from the frame clock and the pixel, so the wear is the same on every play.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: laser-print
items.title: Laser Print
items.description: A beam that prints the interface in as you scroll. Above the line the page is set; at the line a hot glow, sparks, and a heat shimmer; below it, blank stock. Progress follows the surface's position in the viewport by default, plays once on entry with `mode="auto"`, or takes a `progress` value directly.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: wet-canvas
items.title: Wet Canvas
items.description: The interface as wet paint on a woven ground. A weave and a paper grain sit under the page with their own lighting; moving the pointer drags the paint along the direction of travel, raising glossy ridges that catch the light and slowly dry back flat. The drag lives in a small map warmed by the pointer, so the shader stays one pass.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: bonfire-edge
items.title: Bonfire Edge
items.description: Fire along the bottom edge of the interface: flames that rise and lick, sparks that climb and die, and a heat shimmer that bends the page just above them. The flames lean with the pointer and grow where it comes near. Draws only the fire and the shimmer, so the rest of the page is itself.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: flame-border
items.title: Flame Border
items.description: A ring of fire around an element, following its rounded corners. Flames lick inward from every edge with a warm glow on the interior; the middle of the page stays untouched. The border reads the host's corner radius, so it fits whatever shape it wraps.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: fluid-wash
items.title: Fluid Wash
items.description: The interface under a sheet of fluid that the pointer stirs. A real velocity field on the GPU — advected, pressure-solved, dissipating — bends the page where it flows and washes a tint of colour along the current. Runs in half-float where the browser offers it and drops to byte buffers with fewer iterations where it does not.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: glyph-sweep
items.title: Glyph Sweep
items.description: A transition between panels: change the index and a band of glyphs sweeps across the surface, dissolving the old panel into characters at its leading edge and setting the new one in crisp behind it. Both panels are painted textures, so the sweep is one shader pass; between sweeps the surface is the live panel.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: type-rain
items.title: Type Rain
items.description: Streams of glyphs fall over the interface and light it as they pass: the page is held dim, and where a stream crosses, the real colour and type show through around a bright head glyph. Every stream is seeded by its column, so the rain falls the same way each visit. The pointer parts the streams.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: sand-scroll
items.title: Sand Scroll
items.description: The interface dissolves into sand below a line and reassembles as you scroll. Grains stream down and drift from their home pixels, further the deeper they sit below the line, and settle back into crisp type as the line passes. Progress follows the surface's place in the viewport, plays once, or takes a value directly.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: cloth-drape
items.title: Cloth Drape
items.description: The interface as a hanging cloth. A grid mesh carries the painted page; wind rolls slow waves through it, the cursor pushes a dent that springs back, and the shading follows the folds. The mesh is a few thousand vertices, so the drape costs almost nothing.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: cube-fold
items.title: Cube Fold
items.description: The interface folds over cube edges as it scrolls. The top and bottom bands of the page hinge away in perspective as the surface enters and leaves the viewport, meeting flat in the middle of the scroll. One mesh, two hinges, real perspective.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: tile-wave
items.title: Tile Wave
items.description: The interface cut into tiles that tilt and lift as the cursor passes, a wave rolling out from the pointer and settling on springs. Each tile is a quad on a grid mesh with its own centre, so it rotates about itself; gaps between tiles show the ground behind. A click sends a ring through the whole grid.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: hex-floor
items.title: Hex Floor
items.description: The interface laid over a floor of hexagonal prisms seen from a slight angle. Each prism stands at a seeded height and breathes with a slow wave; near the cursor they flatten, so the page reads clearly wherever you look and stands in relief everywhere else.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: glass-shards
items.title: Glass Shards
items.description: The interface as a pane broken into shards. Each shard tilts toward the cursor and refracts what is behind it a little differently from its neighbours, with a bright edge along every crack; near the pointer, shards lift and part, and the ground shows through the gaps. The fracture is a seeded cell pattern, so the pane breaks the same way every time.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ascii-figure
items.title: ASCII Figure
items.description: A 3D figure set in type: the lit render becomes a grid of glyphs chosen by luminance, in one colour, floating and rocking, and yours to orbit by dragging. A torus knot by default; any GLB, glTF, SVG, or image by URL. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: dither-figure
items.title: Dither Figure
items.description: A 3D figure in ordered dither: the lit render quantised through a Bayer matrix into a two-colour palette at a chosen pixel size, floating and rocking, yours to orbit. Retro on purpose and exact about it. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: ink-figure
items.title: Ink Figure
items.description: A 3D figure drawn in ink: silhouette and crease lines from the depth and normal buffers, hatching that darkens with shade, on paper. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: glass-figure
items.title: Glass Figure
items.description: A 3D figure in glass: transmission, refraction, and dispersion through a physical material over a studio backdrop, so the figure bends what sits behind it. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: liquid-figure
items.title: Liquid Figure
items.description: A 3D figure seen through liquid: the render is distorted by a flowing field that the cursor stirs, with a specular sheen on the ripples. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: particle-figure
items.title: Particle Figure
items.description: A 3D figure as points on its surface: thousands of particles that hold the shape, scatter from the cursor, swirl, and spring home. Floats and rocks, yours to orbit. The 3D runtime loads lazily after mount.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: thermal-lens
items.title: Thermal Lens
items.description: A lens that reads the interface as heat: luminance becomes an ironbow palette — black through purple, red, orange, to white-hot — with a soft bloom on the hottest type and a cold blue ground, inside a feathered circle that follows the cursor. Outside it the page is itself.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: negative-lens
items.title: Negative Lens
items.description: An x-ray lens: inside the circle the interface inverts to a negative with bone-white edges lifted from the texture, a faint radiograph grain, and a soft blue cast; the rest of the page stays positive. The edges come from the painted texture, so type reads as structure rather than as a smear.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: blueprint-lens
items.title: Blueprint Lens
items.description: A lens that turns the interface into a cyanotype blueprint: a Prussian-blue ground with the page's edges drawn as fine white lines, a drafting grid behind, and dimension ticks along the rim. Inside the circle the page is a drawing of itself; outside it is the page.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: halftone-lens
items.title: Halftone Lens
items.description: A lens that prints the interface as a four-colour halftone: cyan, magenta, yellow, and black dot screens at their classic angles, so overlaps form the rosette you see in a magazine under a loupe. Dot size follows each channel's density; the paper shows between dots.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: nightscope-lens
items.title: Nightscope Lens
items.description: A night-vision lens: inside the circle the interface is amplified into a green phosphor image with intensifier noise, a soft bloom on bright type, a faint scanline, and a dark vignette at the rim; a mono readout on the rim shows the pointer position. Outside it, daylight.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: comic-lens
items.title: Comic Lens
items.description: A lens that redraws the interface as a comic panel: colours posterised to a few flat tones, black ink outlines lifted from the texture's edges, and Ben-Day dots in the mid tones. Inside the circle the page is drawn; outside it is the page.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: kaleido-lens
items.title: Kaleido Lens
items.description: A kaleidoscope on the cursor: inside the circle the interface is mirrored into six wedges around the pointer, rotating slowly, so a heading becomes a mandala of itself. The mirror geometry is exact, so seams meet without a gap.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: pixel-sort-lens
items.title: Pixel Sort Lens
items.description: A lens that pixel-sorts the interface: within the circle, runs of pixels along the sort axis are dragged into luminance order, so type streaks into bright-to-dark ribbons. The streak length follows the local contrast, and the sort is a deterministic approximation done in one pass.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: reading-ruler
items.title: Reading Ruler
items.description: A reading aid: a horizontal band follows the cursor and keeps the current line crisp and warm while everything above and below softens and dims. The band snaps to the line height under the pointer, read from the real DOM, so it always frames a whole line of type.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: braille-lens
items.title: Braille Lens
items.description: A lens that embosses the interface into raised dots: the page is sampled in six-dot cells and each dot rises where there is ink, lit from the upper left so the dome reads as relief on paper. A quiet, tactile way to see the page as texture.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: soap-film
items.title: Soap Film
items.description: A soap film stretched over the interface: thin-film interference colours drift across the page as the film's thickness flows, and the pointer thins it where it pushes. The colour is computed from the simulated thickness, so it has the true rainbow order of a real film.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: marble-vein
items.title: Marble Vein
items.description: The interface set into polished marble: a seeded vein pattern runs under the page, a soft polish sheen follows the pointer, and the ink sits in the stone as if inlaid. The veins are fixed; the sheen moves.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: crushed-foil
items.title: Crushed Foil
items.description: The interface printed on crushed foil: a seeded crease field gives the surface facets that catch a light that follows the pointer, so highlights sweep across the page as you move. The creases never change; the light does.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: prism-split
items.title: Prism Split
items.description: The interface split into a spectrum along the direction from the pointer: red leads, violet trails, and the fan widens with distance so the far side of the page smears into rainbow while the near side stays sharp. Move, and the fan swings with you.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: honey-glass
items.title: Honey Glass
items.description: The interface under a sheet of honey: the refraction lags the pointer, pools where it rests, and relaxes slowly after it leaves, with a warm amber tint and a specular sheen on the bulge. The lag is a spring with heavy damping — viscosity as motion, not as a filter.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: reeded-glass
items.title: Reeded Glass
items.description: The interface behind reeded glass: vertical flutes refract the page into repeating slivers, a highlight runs down each rib, and the pointer shifts the phase so the slivers slide as you move. A privacy glass that still shows the shape of things.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: mercury-pool
items.title: Mercury Pool
items.description: The interface reflected in a pool of mercury: a chrome surface with a sky-to-ground reflection gradient, ripples that spread from the pointer, and the page floating on it as ink in the metal. The ripples are a real height-field wave; the metal is a reflection model.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: lens-flare
items.title: Lens Flare
items.description: An anamorphic flare drawn from the brightest parts of the interface toward the cursor: horizontal streaks, a few ghost discs along the line, and a soft bloom, all sourced from the page's own highlights. Draws only the light, so the page stays itself.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: oil-slick
items.title: Oil Slick
items.description: The interface under an oil slick: iridescent bands drift over the page with the slow swirl of oil on water, colour ordered by thickness, and a faint reflection of light on the surface. It never repeats and never randomises; the swirl is a flow field on the clock.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: amber-set
items.title: Amber Set
items.description: The interface set in amber: a warm translucent block with inclusions — tiny bubbles and flecks — that drift very slowly, a refraction that thickens toward the edges, and a glow where light enters from above. Everything is preserved; nothing moves fast.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: crt-screen
items.title: CRT Screen
items.description: The interface on a cathode-ray tube: the page curves toward the corners, scanlines and a phosphor triad sit over it, bright type blooms, and the picture breathes with a faint flicker and a slow rolling bar. A click powers it off and on again with the collapse to a line.

items.author: Dragoon (0xDragoon) <https://x.com/0xDragoonLab>
items.name: film-reel
items.title: Film Reel
